name: Kaleidoscopic Animation
visualIdentity: A centered pattern built from a deliberate number of mirrored sectors. Rotation and shape changes develop while symmetry, focal center, density and palette stay coherent. The label is normalized from an explicit kaleidoscope effect.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to psychedelic and demoscene imagery, infinite zooms, surreal spatial passages, ambient visuals and VJ loops. For interactive HTML, finite scroll progress can control a passage or chapter handoff when the subject benefits from it; this is an inferred adaptation.
limitations: Avoid dense text during travel, repeated text in sectors, center jumps and rapid flicker. Adapt or omit when stable orientation or reduced motion is needed, or an unplanned reset would break a one-shot. Keep required chapter passages meaningful; a decorative spiral alone is insufficient.
palette: Optional new-artwork suggestion: background #201D32; foreground #F4E8D4; accents #9E7FB9, #5EA7A0 and #D8A169. These are not canonical. Exact task, brand or reference colors and role assignments take precedence; preserve approved families and limits. Use discrete tokens; gradients are disabled. Check actual composited contrast.
motionAndInteraction: Keep a fixed center and symmetry parameters; derive rotation and phase from shared, seekable time. For interactive output, finite scroll may scrub a vortex passage or chapter transition, with coherent reverse states. Preserve reading holds and limit motion intensity; video must not depend on live input.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied choices. Audio may follow rotation accents or section boundaries, but must leave speech and reading clear. Synchronize and review picture and sound together.
assetRequirements: Use authorized source assets and exact copy; required asset types are unspecified. Canvas 2D, WebGL and GLSL are recommended for mirrored rendering and procedural imagery. Seed randomness, load local fonts/assets, and expose deterministic states or baked frames. HyperFrames assembles and exports video; Remotion is a documented conditional fallback.
combinations: Works alone for ambient visuals. Pair with style-105 timing for beat-mapped rotation and sector changes in music visuals or VJ loops, keeping fixed center and avoiding flicker. Pair with style-006 stepped geometric ornament or sunbursts for gala loops; use gold as an accent and avoid indiscriminate sparkle. Optional motion candidates require scene-level fit.
productionApproach: Choose renderer and motion method by visual fidelity first; GLSL can own the shader motion. Keep one owner per animated property and drive video from composition time for direct, backward and sequential seeks. Use HyperFrames for timing, synchronization, validation and export; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation requires it, documenting the reason. For HTML, map input to bounded progress and support applicable keyboard, touch and reduced-motion behavior. Inspect representative frames and the full delivered video.
